topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Primes and Geometry
target_audience: Undergraduate students with a background in basic calculus

sections.title: The Infinite Sum: Building the Foundation
lecture_lines: The Zeta function sums inverse powers of integers.
For Re(s) > 1, the series converges nicely.
But for s=1, it diverges to infinity.
animations: Show partial sums approaching 2 using '#FFFF00' points.
Highlight the limit process using '#FF0000' frame.

sections.title: Euler’s Bridge: Connecting to Prime Numbers
lecture_lines: Euler discovered a link to prime numbers.
His product formula connects sums and primes.
Primes act as the atoms of numbers.

sections.title: Analytical Continuation: The Magic of Symmetry
lecture_lines: The sum is only valid for Re(s) > 1.
Analytic continuation extends the function further.
It reveals structure across the complex plane.

sections.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The $1 Million Mystery
lecture_lines: The critical strip holds unknown zeros.
Riemann conjectured zeros lie on one line.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Impact
lecture_lines: Primes are key to digital security.
The Zeta function remains a deep mystery.
animations: Show visual graph of prime distribution in '#00FFFF'.
